project.name: HDF5
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/hdf5` is on commit `966454aac1231da7209ef81c11055d3312181f99`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` / `H5O__prefix_deserialize()` / `H5O__chunk_deserialize()` code shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521342 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target h5_extended_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521342
bug_description.normalized: The saved HDF5 witness drives the vulnerable object-header cache parser in `src/H5Ocache.c`. `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` enters `H5O__prefix_deserialize()` without passing the current cache-image bound, so attacker-controlled object-header bytes determine `chunk0_size`; the metadata cache then rereads `actual_len` bytes and `H5O__chunk_deserialize()` materializes an `oh->mesg[]` table whose `id -> mesg->type` / `flags` fields are trusted as real metadata. That table is later queried as a superblock-extension `FSINFO` message, and the decoded `fs_addr[]` values seed an on-disk free-space-manager open. The free-space-manager header at that address supplies a bogus `max_sect_size`, `H5FS__sinfo_new()` sizes the in-memory `bins` array from that bogus value, and close-time superblock-extension allocation then returns a real fragment section to the undersized manager. `H5FS__sect_link_size()` computes `bin = H5VM_log2_gen(sect->size)` and immediately reads `sinfo->bins[bin]` with only an `HDassert(bin < sinfo->nbins)` guard, producing the saved 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/H5FSsection.c:973` during `H5Fclose()`.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled object-header bytes and begins materializing vulnerability-relevant prefix state (`version`, layout flags, and later `chunk0_size`) from the on-disk cache image.
source.value_from: The attacker-controlled bytes come from the saved witness file at `gt_results/arvo_42521342/poc`. The staged run proves this object-header cache path was reached: the HDF5-DIAG prelude records `H5O_msg_exists -> H5O_protect -> H5C__load_entry -> H5O__cache_get_final_load_size -> H5O__prefix_deserialize` before the final ASan crash.
source.note: This anchor points at the first prefix-dispatch statement; the matching fine-trace step covers both the v2 and legacy prefix branches because either path consumes file bytes into `version` / layout state and `chunk0_size`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `bin` is computed from the real fragment section size, but the `bins` array extent was derived earlier from attacker-controlled free-space-manager metadata, so this read lands past the allocated array.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report is `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/H5FSsection.c:973` in `H5FS__sect_link_size`, with the `bins` array allocated by `H5FS__sinfo_new()` at line 146.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The cache callback already knows the speculative `image_len`, but the vulnerable call discards that bound and enters the variable-length object-header prefix parser without passing it. The fix changes this call to `H5O__prefix_deserialize((const uint8_t *)image, image_len, udata)` and then adds explicit `H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(...)` checks inside the prefix/chunk decoders.
root_cause.note: This is the first missing obligation repaired by the patch. Once the callee loses `image_len`, all later prefix field reads and the derived `chunk0_size` trust only attacker-controlled bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: Metadata-cache callback where the raw on-disk object-header image from the malicious HDF5 file and its speculative cache length first enter the vulnerable object-header parser.

parser_admitted.description: The saved run reached the object-header cache parser before the close-time crash: the HDF5-DIAG prelude records this callback and its callee `H5O__prefix_deserialize()` on the staged witness.

coarse_trace.summary: The object-header cache drops the current image-length bound before prefix parsing, trusts attacker-derived `chunk0_size` to compute `actual_len`, and rereads that many bytes for full deserialize.

Chunk-0 parsing recomputes the chunk extent from `chunk0_size`, copies that cache image, and materializes `oh->mesg[]`, including each message's class pointer and flags, from attacker-controlled bytes.

A parsed `FSINFO` message is treated as legitimate superblock-extension metadata only when the stored message class matches `H5O_FSINFO_ID` and the flags do not mark it unknown; decoding then seeds persistent `fs_addr[]`.
The free-space manager opened from that `fs_addr` trusts on-disk header fields such as `max_sect_size`, which then determine the in-memory section-bin array extent.

Close-time superblock-extension allocation returns a real fragment section to the undersized free-space manager, and `H5FS__sect_link_size()` reads past `sinfo->bins` when binning that section by size.

fine_trace.code:
/* Deserialize the object header prefix */
if (H5O__prefix_deserialize((const uint8_t *)image, udata) < 0)
fine_trace.note: Root cause. This callback already has the current cache-image bound in `image_len`, but the vulnerable call drops that bound and enters the variable-length prefix parser with only the raw pointer. The fix passes `image_len` here and adds explicit overflow checks in the callee.

Source. This parser consumes the raw object-header prefix to choose the v2-vs-legacy layout and materialize the prefix state that controls later deserialization, including `chunk0_size`. In the vulnerable tree these reads are driven entirely by file bytes because step 1 did not provide a parser-visible length bound.
The metadata cache trusts the attacker-derived `chunk0_size` from step 2 to compute `actual_len`, the full object-header image size it must reread before chunk-0 deserialize can proceed.

The metadata cache retries deserialize with a buffer of `len` bytes; the function comment states `H5C__load_entry()` reruns deserialize with the correct size after the speculative read, so step 3's `actual_len` becomes this `len`. That same retry passes `udata->chunk0_size` and the full reread buffer into chunk parsing.

Using `chunk_size = udata->chunk0_size` from step 4, the chunk parser recomputes `oh->chunk[0].size`, checks that the reread buffer `len` covers it, copies exactly that many bytes into `oh->chunk[0].image`, and positions `chunk_image` after the already-decoded prefix.

With `chunk_image` inside the copied chunk, the parser reads each message header (`id`, `mesg_size`, `flags`, optional `crt_idx`), bounds it against `eom_ptr`, appends a new `oh->mesg[]` entry, and stores the message's raw payload pointer, payload size, and flags.

The parsed numeric `id` from step 6 is converted into the stored message-class pointer used by later object-header lookups. Unknown IDs are forced to the generic unknown class and may gain `H5O_MSG_FLAG_WAS_UNKNOWN`; known IDs store `mesg->type = H5O_msg_class_g[id]`.

The superblock-extension open path asks `H5O_msg_exists()` and `H5O_msg_get_flags()` for `H5O_FSINFO_ID`. Those helpers load the object header, scan `oh->mesg[]` until `H5O_msg_class_g[H5O_FSINFO_ID] == oh->mesg[idx].type`, and return `idx_msg->flags`; this path only continues when such an entry exists and it is not marked unknown.

After step 8 selects a known FSINFO entry, the decoder reads `vers` and dispatches to either the mapped v0 format or the v1+ format. In the v0 arm, only `H5F_FILE_SPACE_ALL_PERSIST` sets `fsinfo->persist = TRUE` and decodes `fsinfo->fs_addr[]`; in the v1+ arm, the address loop runs only when the stored `persist` byte is nonzero. Non-persistent paths leave `fsinfo->fs_addr[]` as `HADDR_UNDEF`.

The file object copies the per-manager addresses materialized by step 9 into `f->shared->fs_addr[]`. Any slot that step 9 left `HADDR_UNDEF` stays undefined here, while defined slots become the persistent free-space-manager addresses consulted later on file close.

Close-time allocation opens an existing persistent free-space manager whenever `fs_addr[fs_type]` is defined. This selects the on-disk header path seeded in step 10 instead of the fresh-manager path that would initialize `max_sect_size = f->shared->maxaddr`.
The defined `fs_addr[type]` from step 10 is passed straight into `H5FS_open()`, so the library protects and deserializes the free-space-manager header stored at the attacker-selected on-disk address.
The free-space-manager header opened from step 12's on-disk address is trusted to supply `max_sect_size`, the maximum section size this manager claims it can bin.

The attacker-controlled `fspace->max_sect_size` from step 13 determines how many size bins are allocated for the in-memory section-info table. ASan's allocation stack identifies this `bins` allocation as the victim object.

While `H5Fclose()` is creating or recreating the superblock extension, paged allocation produces a real fragment section of size `frag_size` and returns it to the already-open free-space manager. The saved ASan crash stack passes through this exact `H5MF__add_sect` call at line 934.

Sink. The real fragment size from step 15 is converted to a bin index, but the only bound check is a debug-only `HDassert`. Because step 14 sized `sinfo->bins` from the bogus `max_sect_size`, `bin` lands past the 1992-byte array and reading `sinfo->bins[bin].bin_list` matches the saved 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow.

sanitizer_ground_truth.trace_format: HDF5-DIAG prelude plus ASan text report

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the downstream `bins` array in `H5FS__sinfo_new`; the patch repairs the upstream object-header parser in `src/H5Ocache.c` that seeds the bogus free-space-manager state.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The sink-side `H5FS__sect_link_size -> H5MF__alloc_pagefs -> H5F__super_ext_create` portion is directly present in the saved ASan stack. The earlier `H5Ocache -> FSINFO -> fs_addr[]` portion is source-grounded and is the only file-open path that seeds persisted free-space-manager addresses from on-disk object-header bytes.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The attacker-controlled object-header bytes reach the sink as the decoded free-space-manager metadata chain `chunk0_size -> oh->mesg[] -> fsinfo.fs_addr[] -> fspace->max_sect_size -> sinfo->nbins`, which makes a later legitimate `sect->size` produce an out-of-range bin index.

poc.trigger: Open the saved HDF5 witness read-write with the staged `h5_extended_fuzzer`. The dataset-open attempt emits HDF5 object-header decode errors, and `H5Fclose()` later crashes in `H5FS__sect_link_size()` while settling free-space-manager state and creating or recreating the superblock extension.

format.name: HDF5 file
format.contract: This Stage-02 GT is grounded to the exact saved witness file at `gt_results/arvo_42521342/poc` (1808 bytes in the staged artifacts). No broader family of malformed object-header layouts, FSINFO messages, or free-space-manager headers was dynamically validated here.
